ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are all on the grid points of the graph paper. What is the value of $\sin C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Let the length of each small square in the grid be 1,\\
thus CD=3, and AD=4,\\
$\therefore$ in $\mathrm{Rt}\triangle ACD$, we have $AC=\sqrt{AD^{2}+CD^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5$\\
In $\mathrm{Rt}\triangle BCD$, $CB=\sqrt{BD^{2}+CD^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+3^{2}}=\sqrt{10}$\\
As shown in the figure below, draw a perpendicular from point C to AB, and let it intersect the extension of AB at point D. Let AF=4, connect BF, which intersects AC at E,\\
In $\triangle FAB$ and $\triangle ADC$,\\
$\because$ AF=DA=4, $\angle FAB=\angle ADC=90^\circ$, AB=DC=3,\\
$\therefore \triangle FAB \cong \triangle ADC$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore \angle F=\angle CAD$, FB=AC=5\\
$\because \angle FBA=\angle ABE$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABE \sim \triangle FBA$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEB=\angle FAB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AB}{EB}=\frac{FB}{AB}$, that is $\frac{3}{EB}=\frac{5}{3}$\\
$\therefore EB=\frac{9}{5}$\\
$\therefore \sin C= \frac{BE}{BC}=\frac{\frac{9}{5}}{\sqrt{10}}=\boxed{\frac{9\sqrt{10}}{50}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is triangle ABC on grid paper; A and B are on the same horizontal grid line, and AB spans 3 small squares horizontally; C is to the upper right of B, viewed from A it is 4 squares to the right and 3 squares up, and viewed from B it is 1 square to the right and 3 squares up. Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let the side length of each small square be 1, and take A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(4,3). The two vectors starting from C are CA=A-C=(-4,-3), CB=B-C=(-1,-3). Their lengths are respectively |CA|=sqrt(4^2+3^2)=5, |CB|=sqrt(1^2+3^2)=sqrt(10). The sine of angle C can be found using the two-dimensional cross product formula: sin C=|CA x CB|/(|CA||CB|). The magnitude of the cross product is |(-4)(-3)-(-3)(-1)|=|12-3|=9. Therefore sin C=9/(5sqrt(10))=9sqrt(10)/50.
